answers.explanation: Threads share their process's memory, so any thread can read or write any variable.
Threads share one process. Processes are the unit of isolation.
Threads skip setting up a new address space.
A context switch can happen between any two instructions, and your code doesn't get a say.
Parallelism needs tasks executing at the same instant on different cores.
The GIL limits parallelism, not concurrency. Threads still interleave, so races happen in Python too.
Processes have separate address spaces, which is the point of using them.
